parole.testo: From Old Persian, from Proto-Iranian, from Proto-Indo-Iranian. Cognate with Sanskrit आस्तर (āstara).

parole.significato: Expresses the indirect object: to; for
parole.testo: From Middle Persian 𐭯𐭥𐭭 (pʿn) / PWN (pad, “to, at, in, on”), from Old Persian 𐎱𐎫𐎡𐎹 (p-t-i-y /⁠patiy⁠/), from Proto-Iranian *pati-. Northern Luri ڤە (ve).

Inherited from Old Persian *r̥šah, from Proto-Iranian *Hŕ̥šah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hŕ̥ćšas, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ŕ̥tḱos. parole.significato: to have; to possess, to own

From دنگ (“knee”), derived from Old Persian *danu-, from Proto-Iranian *jā́nu. Doublet of زنگار. Compare زانو (“knee”), Ossetian зӕнг (zæng, “shin”).

Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (sh /⁠sē̆⁠/), from Old Persian *çayaʰ, from Proto-Iranian *θráyah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *tráyas, from Proto-Indo-European *tréyes. Indo European cognates include Avestan 𐬚𐬭𐬌- (θri-), Northern Kurdish sê, Pashto درې (dre), Sanskrit त्रि (tri), Greek τρ

From Old Persian *θūryas (“banquet, feast”), from Proto-Iranian *cuHryás, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćuHryás, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱewH- (“to shine”), see also Sanskrit श्वस् (śvas, “tomorrow”). Possibly further related to Northern Kurdish sor (“red”).

From Middle Persian [script needed] (LYLYA), [script needed] (šp /⁠šab⁠/), from Old Persian 𐎧𐏁𐎱 (xšap-), from Proto-Iranian *xšáfš, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kšáps, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷséps. Cognate of Sanskrit क्षप् (kṣap).

parole.significato: a suffix indicating ownership in compound words
parole.testo: From the present stem of داشتن (dâštan, “to have”). See there for further details.
From Old Persian *nipitah, from Proto-Iranian, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *pHtás (compare Sanskrit निपीत (nipīta, “drunk up, imbibed”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₃-.
